newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Swine fever found among Dutch pigs sent to Italy.
newsitem.headline: Swine fever found among Dutch pigs sent to Italy.

text.p: Swine fever has been detected among Dutch piglets exported to Italy earlier this month, a Dutch agriculture ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
The spokesman said it was the first confirmed case of infected pigs being exported to another country following the recent outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands.
The pigs were exported to a farm in the province of Perugia and came from the same area of the southern Netherlands where 24 cases of swine fever have been discovered this month, he said.

The piglets were exported on February 6, two days after the first outbreak of the disease in the Netherlands, but before the European Union imposed a ban on the export of live pigs from this country on February 12, he said.
The European Union decided to extend the ban for a week last Wednesday and its veterinary committee will meet again tomorrow to reconsider the measure.
Since the committee last met the number of cases in the Netherlands has risen from 18 to 24.

The disease and the EU export ban are a serious setback for the Netherlands which annually exports almost a million tonnes of pigs and pork products, bringing in around 5.1 billion guilders ($2.7 billion) a year in export earnings.
Germany is the main foreign market for Dutch pigs and pork products taking 38 percent of all exports, followed by Italy (22 percent), Britain (11 percent) and France (eight percent).

The Dutch have already destroyed tens of thousands of pigs from infected or neighbouring farms and have banned the transport of livestock in a 10 km (six mile) radius of those farms, all located in the southern province of Brabant.
Several cases of swine fever have also been reported in Germany in recent weeks.
